name: Invoice Capture and Coding
title: Invoice Capture and Coding
answer: Invoice capture and coding covers turning supplier invoices, whether paper, PDF, or email, into structured payables records and assigning accounting codes such as general ledger account, cost center, tax treatment, and approval route. It sits between document intake and payment run, and includes line item extraction, purchase order matching, duplicate detection, and exception routing. The goal is to reduce manual keying and coding while keeping the accountant in control of final posting.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Invoice capture and coding covers turning supplier invoices, whether paper, PDF, or email, into structured payables records and assigning accounting codes such as general ledger account, cost center, tax treatment, and approval route. It sits between document intake and payment run, and includes line item extraction, purchase order matching, duplicate detection, and exception routing. The goal is to reduce manual keying and coding while keeping the accountant in control of final posting.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work usually runs on cloud document processing pipelines connected to an ERP or accounting system. Incoming files are stored in a document queue, then passed through optical character recognition and machine learning models, with results written back to the payables module. Many deployments use a human review screen for low confidence fields, and the system logs every prediction for audit.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Modern systems combine optical character recognition with models trained on invoice layouts and chart of accounts history. The model reads header fields such as vendor, invoice number, date, and total, then maps line items to expense or inventory accounts using past coding patterns. Confidence scores flag uncertain fields for review, and feedback from corrected codes retrains or updates the mapping over time.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Because coding affects tax, budgets, and financial statements, the main risks are misclassification, duplicate payment, and fraud. Controls typically require segregation of duties, approval thresholds, and a clear audit trail from original document to posted entry. Data protection rules also apply to vendor bank details and personal data on invoices, so access and retention should follow the same policies as the underlying payables process.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction is toward more end to end automation, where the system proposes not just the code but the full journal entry and payment timing. Better language models are improving extraction from unusual layouts and nonstandard terms, while tighter ERP integration allows coding suggestions to learn from company specific corrections. The likely outcome is fewer manual keystrokes, with staff time shifting to exceptions, vendor disputes, and policy review.
